transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you here today?

Well, thank you so much for seeing me, Doctor. I really appreciate it. I hope I’m not wasting your time... I know you have patients with much worse problems than me. 

It's just, well, things have been a little difficult at my warehouse job lately. They changed my hours around, and they put in this complicated new inventory system. I've always been a hard worker and I usually keep up just fine, but... I hate to even admit this, I feel a little embarrassed saying it out loud... but I feel like I’m just sort of falling apart. 

I’ve actually been missing some shifts, which isn't like me at all, and I've been skipping out on my church commitments too. I've even been snapping at my family, and they certainly don't deserve that. It's gotten to where some mornings I just sit there on the edge of the bed in my work boots, just... wondering if I can even face going into the place anymore. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining things okay for you.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Well, let's see... I'd say it's been about five months now. It started right around the time they brought in that new schedule and the new inventory system at the warehouse. 

I really thought I'd have gotten the hang of it by now, you know? I feel a little silly that it's been going on this long. I usually adapt much quicker than this. Am I giving you the kind of information you need, Doctor? I want to make sure I'm being helpful.
Have you noticed that you’re not enjoying things as much as you used to, like activities you normally like doing?

Well, I... I wouldn't say I've stopped enjoying things completely. I mean, I still like my life, I really do. I'm very blessed. It's just... 

I guess I haven't been doing my usual hobbies quite as much lately. Like my woodworking in the garage... I usually spend a lot of time out there, but I just haven't had the energy for it. And I mentioned missing church... I always look forward to Sunday service and seeing everyone, but lately it just feels like... like a bit too much effort to get dressed and go. 

I feel terrible admitting that, I really do. It sounds so ungrateful, doesn't it? I know I should be doing these things. I'm trying to get back into the swing of it, I promise. Is it normal to feel this way when work gets stressful? I hope I'm not making too big a deal out of nothing.
Have you noticed feeling down, depressed, or hopeless most days, even when there’s no specific stressor happening at the time?

Well, no, not exactly. I mean... I wouldn't use words like "depressed" or "hopeless." That sounds so serious, doesn't it? I really don't think it's anything like that. 

I mean, sure, I feel a bit overwhelmed with all the changes at the warehouse, but when I'm just sitting at home, or when it's a good day... I feel fine. I really do. It's really just tied to the job and all the new things they expect us to learn. 

I'm not just walking around sad all the time for no reason. I hope that's the right kind of answer? I just don't want you to think I'm, you know, completely falling apart over nothing. I'm usually a very positive person.
Have you found that you don’t take as much pleasure or interest in things you used to enjoy, even when you’re doing them?

Oh, no, no... it's not like that. If I actually get out there and do it, I still enjoy it just as much. 

Like, if I do manage to get myself to church, or if I force myself to go out to the garage and pick up my tools, I still feel that same spark. I really do. It's just the... the getting started part that's been a little tough lately, just because I'm so worn out from trying to keep up at the warehouse. But once I'm actually doing my hobbies, it's wonderful. I'm still me, you know? 

I hope I'm explaining that right? I really don't want you to think I've lost my appreciation for the good things in my life. I know how lucky I am, and I always try to count my blessings. Am I making sense, Doctor?
Have you been feeling unusually tired or have you noticed a loss of energy most days, even when you haven’t been doing anything particularly strenuous?

Well, I... I wouldn't say "unusually" tired. I mean, I'm 74, so I suppose it's natural to not have the energy of a young man anymore, right? 

I do get a bit worn out, but I really think it's just from all the extra effort at the warehouse. Trying to learn the new inventory system and keep up with the younger guys... it takes a lot out of me. But on my days off, if I'm just resting around the house, I feel okay. I'm not just sitting around exhausted for absolutely no reason. 

I make sure to get my sleep, and I try to eat right. I'm doing my best to take care of myself, I really am. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm just complaining about getting older. It's perfectly normal to be a little tired after a long week of work at my age, isn't it?
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently, like eating more or less than usual or gaining or losing weight without trying?

Well, no, my appetite has been pretty steady. I mean, my wife always makes sure we have a good dinner on the table, and I always eat what she puts in front of me. I wouldn't want her to think I don't appreciate her cooking, you know?

My clothes still fit exactly the same, so I don't think my weight has changed at all. I try to make sure I'm eating enough to keep my strength up for the warehouse. I know how important that is. 

So, no, I haven't noticed anything like that. I'm doing a good job of keeping up with my meals, I promise. That's a good thing, right, Doctor?
Have you been feeling like you’re not good enough, or been overly hard on yourself about not being able to keep up like you used to?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I know I'm not a young buck anymore, and I certainly don't expect to be able to lift boxes like the twenty-somethings do. I'm very realistic about my age. 

I do get a little frustrated sometimes when I can't quite get the hang of the new computer system as fast as I'd like, but I don't beat myself up over it. I just try to remind myself that I'm doing the best I can, and I've always been a hard worker. I've provided for my family all these years, and I'm proud of that. 

I really try to focus on the positive, you know? I don't want to be one of those grumpy old men who just sits around feeling sorry for himself. I'm doing okay in that department, don't you think?
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or on the contrary, feeling restless or fidgety without meaning to?

Well, um... no, I don't think so. I mean, my wife hasn't said anything about me moving like a turtle or anything like that. I try to keep a good pace, especially at the warehouse. You have to, right? You can't just be dragging your feet when there's work to be done. 

And as for being restless... well, I might tap my foot now and then if I'm trying to figure out that new inventory software, but I'm not pacing the floors or jumping out of my skin. I think I'm pretty steady, all things considered. I try to stay calm and collected. That's the right way to handle things, isn't it, Doctor? I don't want to be making a fuss over nothing.
Have you ever felt like life isn't worth living or had thoughts about hurting yourself?

Oh, goodness, no. No, nothing like that. I mean, I know things have been a little stressful lately with all the changes at the warehouse, but I would never... I've got my wife to think about, and my kids, even if they are all grown up now. 

I've always believed you just have to keep pushing forward, you know? Put one foot in front of the other. I'd never want to cause my family any pain or make them think I was giving up. I'm a fighter, always have been. 

So, no, I don't have thoughts like that. I'm just trying to figure out how to adjust to everything. That's a normal way to look at it, right? I'm doing the right thing by just trying to work through it?
